components:
  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type
          description: Full URL that originated the error response.
          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'
          readOnly: true
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The short error title.
          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time
          example: '2024-11-23T13:59:21.3820407Z'
          readOnly: true
        schemaValidationErrors:
          title: Schema validation errors
          description: Validation errors against the OpenAPI schema.
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationMessage'
      required:
        - type
        - title
        - status
        - detail
        - timestamp
        - schemaValidationErrors
    ValidationMessage:
      title: Validation message
      description: Messages describing a validation error.
      type: object
      properties:
        message:
          title: Message
          description: The validation message.
          type: string
          example: "[Path '/lastName'] Instance type (null) does not match any allowed primitive type (allowed: ['string'])"
          readOnly: true
      required:
        - message
      additionalProperties: true
    Specialty:
      title: Specialty
      description: Fields of specialty of vets.
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          title: ID
          description: The ID of the specialty.
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 0
          example: 1
          readOnly: true
        name:
          title: Name
          description: The name of the specialty.
          type: string
          maxLength: 80
          minLength: 1
          example: radiology
      required:
        - id
        - name
    OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The owner's honorific title. Optional; one of MR, MRS, MS or DR.
            When present it is stored and used to compose the owner's 'salutation'.
          type: string
          enum:
            - MR
            - MRS
            - MS
            - DR
          example: DR
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner. Accepted on input for
            backward compatibility (the flat form); on output it is the composed,
            normalized address - the normalized addressLine1 with a single space and
            the normalized addressLine2 appended when addressLine2 is present.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        addressLine1:
          title: Address line 1
          description: The first line of the owner's structured postal address.
            Preferred over the flat 'address' when present; normalized with the same
            rules (trim, collapse whitespace, upper-case, expand common street-type
            abbreviations).
          type: string
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        addressLine2:
          title: Address line 2
          description: The optional second line of the owner's structured postal
            address (unit, apartment, etc.). Normalized like addressLine1 and, when
            present, appended to the composed 'address' after a single space.
          type: string
          maxLength: 255
          example: 'Apt 5'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: The telephone number of the pet owner. Accepts spaces, dashes and
            brackets and an optional leading '+' with country code on input; stored and
            returned in E.164 form (a '+' followed by 8 to 15 digits). A number without a

## Summary

The endpoint is `POST /api/owners`, served by OfficeFloor function pipelines; the response is an `OwnerDto` generated from `openapi.yml` and populated by MapStruct. I added `riskFlag` as a **derived** field (like `identityKey`, `ownerSegment`, `telephoneDisplay`), computed from the owner's already-stored fields so it is recomputed identically on every read.

`riskFlag` is true when **any** of the three signals hold:

1. **Possible duplicate** — the stored `possibleDuplicate` flag (set by `FlagPossibleDuplicate`: soft soundex+postcode match).
2. **City over soft capacity** — the stored `capacityWarning` flag (set by `FlagCapacityWarning`: city already holds 40+ owners, the soft threshold below the hard 50 limit).
3. **Disposable-adjacent email domain** — the email's second-level label matches a known disposable provider (`mailinator`, `tempmail`, `guerrillamail`) but under a non-blocked TLD. (Exactly-blocked `.com` domains are rejected 400 by `RequireEmailDomain` and never persisted, so a *stored* such email is by definition adjacent, not blocked.)

### Changes
- **`openapi.yml`** — added the `riskFlag` boolean (`readOnly`) property to the Owner schema, so the generated `OwnerDto` gets `getRiskFlag`/`setRiskFlag`.
- **`mapper/RiskFlag.java`** (new) — standalone helper `RiskFlag.of(owner)` computing the OR of the three signals, kept out of the mapper interface so MapStruct doesn't treat it as an implicit mapping method (matching `OwnerSegment`/`Locality`).
- **`mapper/OwnerMapper.java`** — added the `riskFlag` expression mapping.

### Tests
`AcceptanceTest.coreRiskFlagFalseNormally` (a fully-unique owner with no email → false) passes, and the full suite is `BUILD SUCCESS` with no regressions.

One judgment call worth flagging: the spec's "disposable-adjacent" wasn't previously defined anywhere in the code (the existing blocklist is for the hard 400 rejection). I defined it as "shares a known disposable provider's second-level label under a non-blocked TLD" and documented that precisely in both the schema description and the helper Javadoc — if you had a different notion of "adjacent" in mind (e.g. Levenshtein distance to a blocked domain, or a broader keyword set), that's the one spot to adjust.
